headline: Waltham School Committee ratifies Building Trades contract, approves high school handbook, Equity Plan, and PROTECT Act policy, and recommends naming 617 Lexington Street building after Jack Daddona
summary: The Committee approved the 2026-2027 Waltham High School student handbook, the Waltham Public Schools 3 year Equity Plan, and a PROTECT Act model policy. It ratified a Memorandum of Agreement with the Waltham Public Schools Building Trades union and voted to recommend the Waltham City Council name the 617 Lexington Street building after former superintendent Jack Daddona. The Committee also approved the consent agenda and paid bills on the warrant.
decisions: Approved moving to Executive Session to discuss collective bargaining and negotiations with several unions and nonunion personnel.
Approved the Consent Agenda including minutes, retirements, and resignations.
Approved hearing from all off-Committee members.
Approved the 2026-2027 Waltham High School student handbook.
Approved the Waltham Public Schools 3 year Equity Plan.
Ratified the Memorandum of Agreement with the Waltham Public Schools Building Trades union.
Recommended that the Waltham City Council name the 617 Lexington Street building 'The John J. "Jack" Daddona Education Center'.
Approved the PROTECT Act Model Policy.
Approved paying the bills on the warrant.

 and / or conduct negotiations with the Waltham School Department Food Service

 Waltham School Building Trades; and to conduct strategy sessions in preparation for 
 negotiations with nonunion personnel and/or to conduct negotiations with nonunion 
 personnel  – Assistant Superintendent for Finance and Operations, to include 
 Attorney Jonathan Atwater, Superintendent Dr. Mendonsa and HR Administrator Kate 
 Peretz, and return to the regular meeting at 7:00 pm.  All in favor. 
 Ms. Wong-Bigelow arrived at 5:39pm during the Executive Session. 
 Mayor McCarthy arrived at 5:58pm during the Executive Session. 
 The School Committee reconvened at 7:11pm.  Present were Mr. Tarallo, Mr. Zanghi, 
 Mrs. Coleman, Mrs. AlJammal, Ms. DeJoannis, Ms. Wong-Bigelow, and Mayor 
 McCarthy.  Mayor McCarthy presided. 
 The Committee recited the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 Mayor McCarthy announced the meeting was being recorded by WCAC. 
 Waltham resident Terry Marks expressed his disapproval of the district’s schools 
 being ranked in the bottom 10% in the state.  He provided examples of his family’s 
 experience with the Waltham Public Schools over the years and urged the district to 
 perform at a higher level as taxpayers are funding the schools through their high tax 
 amounts. 
 Waltham parent Nicole Piche-Nicholas addressed the Committee requesting more 
 concrete information about the high school schedule process.  She stated that 
 logistical updates do not equate to meaningful transparency for the high school 
 community.  She urged the Committee to have the superintendent publicly share all 
 schedule options that are being considered along with the impacts to students. 
 WSAA members Val Alfeo, Robert Lyons, Mary Jo Rendon and Derek Vandegrift, 
 along with WSSA president Krissy Scheufele all urged the Committee members to 
 offer fair and equitable contracts to each of the unions currently working without

 Dr. Mendonsa confirmed it was a successful first day of school for students across 
 the district in grades one through twelve. 
 Information was shared about the district’s new Administrator of Student Engagement 
 and Discipline, Liz Murray; the Director of Counseling, Carolyn Imperato, and Kristin 
 Gentili, the new Food Service Director. 
 The superintendent thanked Cradles to Crayons for donating over 100 backpacks full 
 of supplies for our elementary students. 
 Dr. Mendonsa updated the Committee on the improvement in student attendance 
 between the 2025 and 2026 school years. All schools saw an increase in student 
 attendance and the majority also saw a sharp decline in the rate of chronically absent 
 (10% or more) students last year as well.  Additionally, the rate of chronically absent 
 (20% or more) remained the same or decreased in half of the district.

 Schools.  The amount is lower than the original projection but is expected to increase 
 over the next month. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Mrs. Coleman, to hear from all 
 off-Committee members.  All in favor. 
 Assistant Superintendent for Curriculum and Instruction Dr. Shannon Conley 
 reviewed the proposed changes to the Waltham High School student handbook for 
 this year.  The changes include the updating of language, processes and procedures, 
 the addition of new policies and statutes, and the removal of outdated language or 
 practices no longer utilized.  The introduction section, staff names, contact 
 information, and list of clubs and activities were also updated. 
 Mrs. Coleman left the meeting at 7:52pm and returned at 7:56pm. 
 A discussion between Ms. Wong-Bigelow and Dr. Conley ensued about specific 
 terminology that Ms. Wong-Bigelow requested change.  Dr. Conley indicated any 
 language stemming from a state law or School Committee policy cannot be changed 
 within the handbook. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. AlJammal, seconded by Mrs. Coleman, to approve the 
 2026-2027 Waltham High School student handbook.  All in favor. 
 The superintendent reminded the group that the district’s proposed three year Equity 
 Plan was presented at the last meeting.  She highlighted key points of the three year 
 process including the priorities, recommendations and plans for action.  Ms. 
 DeJoannis referenced Mrs. AlJammal’s prior request that a definition of “equity” be 
 determined and asked that a definition for “high expectation” also be set forth. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Mr. Tarallo, to approve the 
 Waltham Public Schools 3 year Equity Plan.  All in favor. 
 Dr. Mendonsa advised she plans to review the proposed plans for the 617 Lexington 
 Street building previously provided by the architect. 
 Ms. DeJoannis asked that a more cohesive proposal for 617 be presented to the 
 members for consideration.  Mayor McCarthy added that the type of structure of the 
 building needs to be determined with Dual Language and Valor being priorities, as 
 well as Early Childhood Education. 
 Nothing new was shared in this category.

 Dr. Conard will convene the WHS Schedule Team later this month to continue 
 analyzing schedule options. 
 Mrs. Coleman added that while this is a standing agenda item, it does not mean that 
 a new, detailed update will be provided at each meeting.  She acknowledged that 
 some of the Schedule Committee members did not work over the summer but as this 
 is an ongoing project, updates will be provided when available.  Mayor McCarthy 
 received confirmation that a timeline and feedback sessions will be communicated by 
 Dr. Conard. 
 It was noted that minutes of city department meetings are available online relative to 
 city decisions about new residential property requests. 
 Mrs. Coleman reviewed the evaluation process for the superintendent and confirmed 
 she received individual written evaluations from all members.   The evaluation is 
 divided into multiple steps, performance goals and standards and the Vice-Chair 
 reviewed the ratings within each area.  She quoted some of the feedback received 
 and advised the full evaluation, complete with Dr. Mendonsa’s written goals, will be 
 posted on the WPS district website. 
 Mrs. AlJammal highlighted the changes in the new 2025-2028 contract with the 
 Building Trades union including an increase in vacation time, an annual salary 
 increase, and the addition of new steps. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. AlJammal, seconded by Mr. Tarallo, to ratify the 
 Memorandum of Agreement with the Waltham Public Schools Building Trades union. 
 All in favor. 
 The members executed the Memorandum of Agreement. 
 Mr. Tarallo shared his thoughts about naming the 617 Lexington Street building after 
 former WPS superintendent Jack Daddona. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to request the 
 Waltham City Council consider the School Committee’s recommendation of naming 
 the 617 Lexington Street building “The John J. ‘Jack’ Daddona Education Center”. 
 All in favor. 
 A short discussion followed about whether the existing schools and programs within 
 the building would retain their current names and identities and it was confirmed they 
 should.
